q: Sub-brokers in India ceased to exist as an intermediary category from:
e: SEBI's Board decision (June 21, 2018) discontinued sub-brokers effective April 1, 2019. All existing sub-brokers had to migrate to Authorised Person status or become trading members.

q: Which of the following can ONLY clear and settle their own proprietary trades and their clients' trades?
e: Self Clearing Member (SCM) is a TM who clears only own + own-client trades. Cannot clear for other TMs. TCM clears for self + other TMs. PCM clears only (no own trading).

q: Order matching in India's F&O segment follows:
e: Best price wins; at the same price, earliest timestamp wins. Partial matches allowed; remainder stays in the book.

o: Stays in the book until end of day
Executes immediately, with unmatched portion cancelled
Is equivalent to a stop-loss order
e: IOC orders execute as much as can be matched immediately; any unmatched portion is cancelled instantly. Partial execution is allowed.

For a sell stop-loss, the trigger must be set above the limit (i.e. trigger > limit) — and trigger must be between the last traded price and limit. When LTP falls to trigger, the order activates as a limit-sell at the limit price.

q: Default trading hours in the equity derivatives segment are:
e: Default derivatives hours are 9:15 AM – 3:30 PM, Mon-Fri. SEBI permits exchanges to extend up to 11:55 PM with adequate risk infra (rarely exercised).

q: To be eligible for stock derivatives, a stock's average daily traded value (ADTV) over the past 6 months must be at least:
e: Per current SEBI norms, ADTV must be ≥ ₹150 cr (within the top 500 by market cap), MWPL ≥ ₹1,250 cr, and quarter-sigma order size ≥ ₹50 lakh.

q: Which corporate role in the trading software has the highest level of access?
e: Corporate Manager → Branch Manager → Dealer is the hierarchy. Only the Corporate Manager can set branch-level exposure limits and view all dealers across all branches.

q: Adjustment of strike price for a stock split is done using:
o: The ratio of price before / price after the split
e: Strike (and lot size) are adjusted by the ratio of pre-action / post-action price. For a 2:1 split, post-price is half, so strike is halved and lot doubled.

q: STT on the sale of equity options is currently:
e: STT on sale of options = 0.10% of the premium (paid by seller). On exercise, the buyer additionally pays 0.125% of the settlement value. Futures sale STT is 0.0125%.

o: SEBI wanted to simplify the broker network and reduce regulatory overlap
e: SEBI rationalised the broker network by abolishing the sub-broker category, requiring all existing sub-brokers to migrate to APs (acting as agents of trading members) or trading members themselves.

q: When a TM hits its position limit, the trading system will:
o: Permit only trades that reduce the existing position
Halt all trading on the exchange
e: Once at the position limit, only reducing trades are allowed. New positions (openers) are blocked even if the TM has surplus margin. Squaring-off is permitted.
